The Review Petition was heard ‘on admission’ on 5.7.2023, and the Commission, after hearing the learned counsel for the Review Petitioner, ‘admitted’ issued notice on ‘admissibility’ with directions to the parties to complete pleadings in the matter. Thereafter, the Review Petition was listed for hearing on various dates viz 8.11.2023, 29.11.2023, 4.4.2024, 23.10.2024, 28.11.2024, 14.1.2025, but was adjourned on each occasion due to various reasons such as requests for adjournment and due to paucity of time, etc. 3. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Review Petitioner and the learned counsel for the Respondent argued the matter at length. The Commission, after permitting the parties to file their short note of arguments, reserved its order in the Review Petition. In compliance thereof, the Review Petitioner and the Respondent NTPC and 4. Based on the submissions of the parties and the documents on record, we proceed - iii.The Review Petitioner has not approached this Commission with clean hands and has disclosed that various appeals have been filed by the Review Petitioner before the APTEL, thereby raising a similar ground. The issue raised by the Review Petitioner in the present Review Petition qua the IoWC on the basis of ‘as billed’ GCV of coal for the period of January 2014 to March 2014 is an issue which falls for consideration in Appeal No. 258 of 2022. - iv.The Review Petitioner has contended that that the Commission has erred while determining the IoWC vide the Order in Review on the basis of the assumed ‘as received’ GCV data for the period of January 2014 to March 2014, in as much as the ‘as received’ GCV data was neither furnished in the Truing Petition nor in the Additional Submissions filed by the Answering Respondent. - v.The contentions raised by the Petitioner are entirely misconceived and devoid of any merits in as much as the Order in Review passed by the Commission while considering the measurement of GCV of Coal on ‘as received’ basis furnished by the Answering Respondent vide its Additional Submissions which is strictly in line with 3rd Amendment to the Tariff Regulations, 2009, read with Regulation 28 of the Tariff Regulation, 2014. - viii.Since NTPC faced implementation challenges, it filed Petition No. 244/MP/2016 seeking removal of difficulties under Regulation 30(6), which remains pending. NTPC, in Petition No. 698/GT/2020 dated 18.1.2020, sought the truing up of the tariff for Farakka Stage I & II for 2014–19 and invoked the relaxation clause under the Tariff Regulations. NTPC also filed additional submissions dated 28.6.2021: - x. NTPC had furnished the requisite details vide its additional submissions dated 28.6.2021 at the stage of adjudication of the trueing petition, which was duly considered by the Commission in the review order. Therefore, once IoWC has already been computed based on actual data furnished by NTPC, the Review Petitioner’s allegation that assumed or inaccurate data was used has no merit. 9. The Review Petitioner vide its rejoinder affidavit dated 22.8.2023, mainly submitted as under: (ii) GRIDCO has also filed Appeal No. 258/2022 before APTEL challenging the truingup order in Petition No. 362/GT/2020, which is pending adjudication. Therefore, the appeal and the present Review Petition relate to different generating stations and separate orders of the Commission. There is no bar to maintaining both, even if the issues involved are similar. # **_Non-consideration of the decision as per the tariff order in the truing-up order:_** (xii) This position was acknowledged by the Commission in Para 29(d) of its order dated 19.2.2016 in Petition No. 33/MP/2014 (relied on by NTPC), where the Commission noted that the absence of sampling and testing facilities on an ‘as received’ basis needs to be addressed. 10. Before we proceed to consider the issue raised by the Review Petitioner, we examine the submissions of Respondent NTPC that the issue raised by the Review Petitioner in the present Review Petition qua the IoWC on the basis of ‘as billed’ GCV of coal for the period of January 2014 to March 2014 is pending consideration of the APTEL in Appeal No. 258 of 2022 filed by the Review Petitioner against the order dated 21.4.2022 passed by this Commission in Petition No. 362/GT/2020. Accordingly, Respondent NTPC has submitted that when an issue which is sub-judice before a superior court, the lower court must refrain from considering the said issue till the adjudication of the matter in its entirety by the superior court. Per contra, the Review Petitioner has contended that the present Review Petition, is maintainable as there is no bar against the filing of appeal and Review Petition against different orders and for different generating stations, even if the issue involved is the same. 11. We have examined the submissions and agree with the submissions of the Review Petitioner in this regard. The pendency of an appeal on this issue before APTEL does not bar the filing and consideration of this issue in a review proceeding related to a Commission’s order, in respect of a different generating station. Accordingly, the objections of the Respondent NTPC on the maintainability of the Review Petition are misconceived. Given that there are no interim orders/directions of APTEL barring the Commission from considering the issue involved herein, which has been raised in the Review Petition, we find no reason to reject the Review Petition as not maintainable. Accordingly, we proceed to examine whether the issue raised by the Review Petitioner is maintainable on merits, as stated in the subsequent paragraphs. rejected by the Commission vide order dated 10.6.2025. In the above background, the submissions of the Review Petitioner and the Respondents, BRPL & BYPL, are rejected, and the Review Petition is accordingly held to be not maintainable. 15.
